record.original_question: What fundamentally new forms of self-organization arise in systems with nonlocality in time and memory, especially when changing memory creates a hierarchy of relaxation times that qualitatively alters the system's behavior?

evidence.quote: The emergence and change of memory can leads to the appearance of hierarchy of relaxation times and qualitatively change the behavior of the systems at the remaining other parameters unchanged.
Similarly, fundamentally new types of self-organization are expected in processes with nonlocality in time and memory.
This direction of future researches is very important for nonlinear fractional dynamics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider dynamical systems whose evolution is nonlocal in time, in the sense that the state x(t) at time t is determined not only by its instantaneous value and local derivatives but also by its full past history through a memory kernel K(t,s). Concretely, consider evolution equations of the form

  (D^{α}_{t} x)(t) = F(x(t), t) + ∫_{0}^{t} K(t,s) G(x(s), s) ds,

where D^{α}_{t} denotes a fractional time derivative of order α ∈ (0,1] (e.g. Caputo or Riemann–Liouville), F and G are nonlinear functions, and K(t,s) is a memory kernel that may itself evolve in time, thereby inducing a hierarchy of distinct relaxation times τ_1 < τ_2 < … < τ_n.

Identify and classify the qualitatively new forms of self-organization (e.g. attractors, coherent structures, pattern formation, synchronization regimes, or phase transitions) that can arise in such systems specifically because of the temporal nonlocality and the time-evolving memory, and which do not occur in their memoryless (local-in-time) counterparts. In particular, characterize how a hierarchy of relaxation times generated by a changing memory kernel qualitatively alters the long-time behaviour and emergent collective states of the system, with all other parameters held fixed.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad open research direction in nonlinear fractional dynamics concerning self-organization in systems with time nonlocality and evolving memory. No general classification or solution appears in the literature; it is posed as a future research direction rather than a precise conjecture, so the status is best described as open.

status_evidence.title: Nonlinear Fractional Dynamics (general literature)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses memory and hierarchy of relaxation times as future research direction in nonlinear fractional dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open future research direction rather than a resolved result.
